# Crypto Lab — algorithm and exhibit catalog

<!-- catalog-sync:begin — generated by tools/catalog-sync.js from index.html cards, tools/catalog-exhibits.json source reviews and tools/catalog-native.json; do not edit by hand -->

The algorithm facts below are generated from `index.html` cards. The card facts
are derived from each lab's own source by
`tools/catalog-evidence.js`, and each implemented algorithm carries the `file:line`
where the evidence is. Source shapes the scanner cannot establish are recorded
in `tools/catalog-reviewed.json` at a pinned lab commit. Specific UI actions and
outcomes come from the separate, source-pinned `tools/catalog-exhibits.json` review.
Nothing in this generated document is edited by hand.

**Implemented** means the lab's code computes it — the algorithm appears in a
declaration, an invocation, a module import, a WebCrypto call, or a pinned source review.
**Referenced** means the lab names it without implementing it: a lab that teaches an
attack on HQC by modelling its decode time references HQC without implementing HQC.
The distinction is the point of the index, and a grep cannot make it.

Regenerate with `node tools/catalog-sync.js`; re-derive the underlying facts with
`node tools/catalog-evidence.js write`; re-check every anchor against the lab clones
with `node tools/catalog-evidence.js verify`.
To extend a section entry, review the lab's current default branch and add
its named control, learner action, computed or displayed result, concepts,
execution status, limits, and source lines to `tools/catalog-exhibits.json`.
Pin the full source commit and set the scope to `selected` unless every
section was checked. Run `node tools/catalog-exhibits.js verify` against
available lab checkouts, then regenerate and check this catalog.
Each lab entry links its pinned source commit. Its `path:line` evidence
anchors refer to that exact revision. Use ranged reads or search by concept
or lab name in this large file.

## Hub-hosted interactive studies

These studies live in this catalog repository rather than a separate lab repository.
Their source anchors refer to this same catalog commit. They are outside the standalone-lab count.

### [Chip transaction authentication](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/learn/emv-chip/)

- **Visible section:** Follow the packet
- **Learner action:** Approve a synthetic card packet, alter its amount, replay it, and compare a different checkout challenge.
- **Observed result:** Observe issuer decisions for matching, modified, repeated, and wrong-checkout packets.
- **Concepts taught:** EMV online-authentication idea; transaction data binding; terminal challenge; replay; card counter
- **Execution:** real-crypto teaching model
- **Limits:** HMAC-SHA-256 over invented fields; not an EMV application cryptogram, test vector, chip command, issuer policy, or offline-authentication implementation.
- **Evidence at this catalog commit:** `learn/emv-chip/index.html:23`, `learn/emv-chip/index.html:30`, `learn/emv-chip/model.mjs:43`, `learn/emv-chip/model.mjs:54`

## Find a concept in an exhibit

Search this document for a concept and read the matching **Concepts taught**
line under its lab entry. That entry names the exact visible section, learner
action, observed result, limitations, and source lines at a pinned commit.
Search the lab source as well when its exhibit map is only partial.
Use these section types when assessing a new paper, book, or standard.
**Interactive** changes a live result;
**comparison** juxtaposes options or outcomes (with controls when available); **explanation** is
text a learner can read, with no interactive implementation implied.
**Execution status** is separate: `real-crypto` runs cryptographic operations;
`real-operation` performs another actual computation (such as image encoding);
`simulation` models behavior; `real-values` visualizes sourced parameters;
`conceptual` walks through an idea without running its cryptographic internals.
A `related` term is context only, never proof that a concept is taught or implemented.
The implementation index farther down answers a different question.

The exhibit map currently records **1768 sections in 245 of 245 labs**
(245 complete lab inventories, 0 selected-section reviews).
**COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW** means all substantive visible sections were inventoried
at the pinned revision; it is not a security audit or a claim about future edits.
**PARTIALLY REVIEWED** means only selected sections were mapped: omission says
nothing about the remaining panels. Every current lab has a source-pinned map. Inspect
their current source before ruling out a concept, including for partial maps.
For a reviewed lab, verify the pinned commit is still its current default branch
before relying on this index for a fresh assessment.

## Overlap report

Pairs of labs that implement the same algorithms, weighted so that sharing a rare
algorithm counts and sharing SHA-256 does not. An overlap is not a fault — two labs
may teach the same primitive from different angles — but an overlap **with no stated
difference** is a question nobody has answered, and a visitor choosing between the
two has nothing to go on.

68 pairs: 10 with a stated difference, **0 examined and found to be duplication**, 58 nobody has looked at.

A pair marked DUPLICATION is a finding, not a description: someone read both and
found no difference worth having. It is listed first because it is the only row here
that asks for a decision.

**HPKE Envelope / Blind Relay**

- **Shared:** ChaCha20, ChaCha20-Poly1305, DHKEM, HKDF, HPKE, Poly1305, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**Frodo Vault / Scloud+ Vault**

- **Shared:** FrodoKEM, LWE, ML-KEM
- **Stated difference:** both are unstructured-LWE KEMs: frodo-vault is FrodoKEM, the conservative plain-LWE design that avoids algebraic structure outright; scloud-vault is Scloud+, which keeps unstructured LWE but adds ternary secrets and Barnes-Wall lattice coding for efficiency

**KDF Chain / KDF Arena**

- **Shared:** Argon2, HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** kdf-chain teaches what problem each KDF solves and walks a decision tree for choosing one; kdf-arena benchmarks the same four side by side and reports attacker cost against wall-clock time

**Factor Forge / Residue Gate**

- **Shared:** Jacobi symbol, Miller–Rabin
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**FROST Threshold / Shamir vs FROST**

- **Shared:** Ed25519, FROST, SHA-512, Shamir secret sharing
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**ZK Arena / Log Forge**

- **Shared:** Baby-step giant-step, Pohlig–Hellman
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**Ratchet Wire / Encrochat**

- **Shared:** AES, AES-GCM, Diffie-Hellman, Double Ratchet, HKDF, SHA-256, X25519
- **Stated difference:** ratchet-wire demonstrates the Double Ratchet working as designed; encrochat reconstructs the 2020 Encrochat takedown, where the same construction was never broken and the endpoint was compromised instead

**Babel Hash / Hash Zoo**

- **Shared:** BLAKE3, SHA-256, SHA-3
- **Stated difference:** Both teach SHA-256/SHA3-256/BLAKE3, avalanche and real length-extension, so substantial overlap remains. Choose Babel Hash for the attack-to-defense sequence: sweep secret-length guesses, then test HMAC-SHA256 against the same attack. Choose Hash Zoo for construction inspection: examine SHA-256 padding and the SHA-3 rate/capacity split beside the Merkle-Damgard, sponge and tree views. Portfolio membership is not the distinction.

**STARK Tower / Polynomial Forge**

- **Shared:** FRI, Merkle tree, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** stark-tower runs a whole STARK, prover and verifier, catching a cheating prover through a FRI low-degree test; polynomial-forge opens the commitment layer underneath and compares KZG, IPA and FRI as schemes in their own right

**Format Ward / Regex Veil — FTE**

- **Shared:** AES, AES-CBC, FF1
- **Stated difference:** format-ward PRESERVES an existing format with FF1 and FF3-1, so ciphertext keeps the length and alphabet of the input; fte TRANSFORMS ciphertext into whatever language a regular expression defines, by ranking a DFA slice

**VSS Gate / Reshare Circle**

- **Shared:** Feldman VSS, Pedersen commitment, Shamir secret sharing
- **Stated difference:** vss-gate adds VERIFIABILITY to Shamir sharing at deal time, through Feldman and Pedersen commitments; reshare-circle leaves the dealing alone and refreshes shares over time, using HJKY proactive sharing against perpetual leakage

**Blind Hello / Blind Relay**

- **Shared:** DHKEM, HPKE
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

## Labs

245 labs. Implementation findings and source coverage are separate questions.

**N/A (7)** — source-reviewed labs that model an attack or
system but implement no named algorithm in this index. N/A is a reviewed
finding, not the automatic scanner's answer to a miss.

**UNKNOWN (0)** — every file this scanner reads was read and no algorithm was
derivable, with no source review resolving whether that is an intentional model or
a missed implementation. Do not treat this as N/A.

**NOT-SCANNED (0)** — the lab implements its cryptography in a language this
scanner does not read, so there is no finding either way. `could not look` is not
`nothing there`, and collapsing the two would publish "implements nothing" about source
nobody opened.

**Partially unread (8)** — some bundled source or binary remains opaque
to this index; the algorithm list is a floor rather than a total.

### Ablation Wire

[`crypto-lab-ablation-wire`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-ablation-wire/) · Layer Ablation · PROTOCOLS, ATTACKS, POST-QUANTUM

The 1942 Navajo code-talker stack rebuilt on modern primitives, with every layer independently switchable — turn one off and discover which was actually load-bearing.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X-Wing KEM, AES-256-GCM, Transcript Binding, Rust/WASM — labels do not establish what any section runs.

[`crypto-lab-accumulator`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-accumulator/) · Cryptographic Accumulators · PROTOCOLS, PRIVACY

One fixed-size digest commits to a growing set. Prove a certificate is in it — or, the hard part, that it is not — with a short witness, then forge one with the trapdoor.

### Adaptor Gate

[`crypto-lab-adaptor-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-adaptor-gate/) · Scriptless Scripts · SIGNATURES, PROTOCOLS

One click turns a pre-signature the real BIP-340 verifier rejects into a valid signature, then subtracts the two to read the secret back out — the fact that atomic swaps and PTLC routing are both built on.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** BIP-340, secp256k1, Atomic Swap, PTLC — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Schnorr `src/crypto/attacks.ts:8`, secp256k1 `src/crypto/adaptor.ts:156`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/vectors.ts:23`
- **Source review:** [f838c41a6708](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-adaptor-gate/commit/f838c41a6708ee52e70e395f394c53b513d31558) — secp256k1 is added by review because the scanner now reads `import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js'` as a module path rather than an implementation, which is right in general and wrong here: src/crypto/secp.ts wraps that import into the lab's own point and scalar layer (N, G, mulG, mul, liftX, invModN) and src/crypto/adaptor.ts computes the adaptor construction on it directly. The anchor is the defining point addition, R + T, not the import. Adaptor layer is the lab's own code over @noble/curves point/scalar ops; the completed signature is verified by the library's unmodified BIP-340 verify. Ledgers and PTLC routing are modeled and labelled as such in-page; PTLC settlement is causal (each hop consumes the value extracted downstream), not precomputed.
- **References:** EC point arithmetic, ECDSA, FROST
- **Attacks shown:** Discrete log `src/ui/honesty.ts:109`, Key recovery `src/ui/honesty.ts:50`, Nonce reuse `src/crypto/attacks.ts:65`

### AES Anatomy

[`crypto-lab-aes-anatomy`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-aes-anatomy/) · Build AES, Then Attack a Fault · ENCRYPTION, ATTACKS

Build AES from field arithmetic through encryption and decryption, break weakened variants, recover a key from structured round-9 DFA, then rank one byte from accepted-output bias in a bounded statistical ineffective fault attack (SIFA) model.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** AES-128/192/256, GF(2⁸), Differential Fault Analysis, Bounded SIFA — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/aes/cipher.ts:6`
- **Source review:** [1f0f6b86a2dd](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-aes-anatomy/commit/1f0f6b86a2dd5b631df13377b5e1a205e712a502) — Reviewed the complete nine-act AES-128/192/256 data path, inverse, key expansion, four opt-in layer ablations, structured round-9 DFA and first-round ineffective-fault lesson. Act 9 executes correct and fault-path AES-128 for each finite-sample trial and classifies exact ciphertext equality; its separate 2,048-row census is analytic, not sampled execution evidence. The selection-only ranker receives selected plaintext bytes and a target bit. A secret-independent null removes key-dependent selection. Rejection exposes output absence; the bounded teaching infection hides selection without a classifier, while an explicitly granted exact clean-reference oracle restores it. The transform is not timing-oblivious, hardened, universal or an implementation of the cited circuit defenses. Side-channel and generic timing mentions remain limits or neighboring labs, not executed attacks. WebCrypto independently checks the hand-written cipher; AES-CBC is an oracle wrapper, not a mode lesson.
- **References:** AEGIS-256, AES-CBC, SHA-256, TLS 1.3

### Agreeing in Public

[`crypto-lab-agreeing-in-public`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-agreeing-in-public/) · Key Agreement Basics · KEY EXCHANGE

The paint-mixing picture, then one real X25519 exchange with both sides&rsquo; secrets compared byte for byte &mdash; and a stranger who answers in Bob&rsquo;s place while every check on the page still passes. No modulus, no exponent.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X25519, RFC 7748, Key Agreement, No Authentication — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** X25519 `src/x25519/agree.ts:64`
- **Source review:** [fc21875bf6c5](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-agreeing-in-public/commit/fc21875bf6c54edae5fb6a83dbd604ae29b579a4) — Read src/x25519/agree.ts, src/eavesdrop/attempt.ts, src/ui/mixing.ts and src/main.ts. The exchange is real @noble/curves X25519 and the lab checks RFC 7748 5.2's published vectors in the browser before anything is pressed. The scanner anchored X25519 at src/eavesdrop/attempt.ts:1, an import line in the eavesdropper module; the pin moves it to getSharedSecret in the agreement module. 'Discrete log' was derived from README prose explaining what is NOT taught here and is removed: the lab says outright that it never uses the words, and hands the mathematics to DH MITM and Key Exchange. The man-in-the-middle anchor stays -- panel 4 really does run a stranger answering in Bob's place, and every check on the page still passes, which is the lab's negative claim rather than a disclaimer.

- **Implements:** AES `src/fabesa/kem.ts:119`, AES-GCM `src/fame/kem.ts:107`, BLS12-381 `src/fabesa/fabesa.ts:29`, Hash-to-curve `src/fabesa/fabesa.ts:200`, HKDF `src/fame/kem.ts:56`, Pairing `src/fame/bls.ts:191`, SHA-256 `src/fame/kem.ts:56`
- **Source review:** [ab293fd0386f](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-attribute-gate/commit/ab293fd0386fac2a4e89cede2b414056df3188eb) — Read the merged README, complete FAME, FABESA, RW15 and epoch-adaptation source, tests, learner interface and visible limitations at this exact main commit. Attribute Gate executes BLS12-381 source-group and target-group arithmetic and pairings but never calls a BLS signing or verification operation; `src/fabesa/fabesa.ts:29` and `src/fame/bls.ts:17` import the `bls12_381` group namespace, so BLS signatures is a scanner false positive and is removed. The README's explicit CCA-security limit is not an executed chosen-ciphertext attack and is removed too. The reviewed pairing anchor points to the actual wrapper at `src/fame/bls.ts:191`, not the counter reset at line 183. The original FAME route still executes public-policy sealing, key issuance, threshold reconstruction, same-authority collusion failure, authority escrow and its native lack of revocation. The separate FABESA route retains its bounded partial policy-hiding profile (values hidden; names, structure, dimensions and lengths public) and theorem limits. The new RW15 route executes two independent authority setups, authority-qualified attributes, byte-exact GID binding, same-GID opening, the strongest raw cross-GID pool and one-issuer compromise; its hybrid record wrapper does not inherit the paper's theorem. The separately labeled epoch lesson is an owner-assisted application adaptation around single-authority FAME, HKDF-SHA-256 and AES-256-GCM: it executes complete-key reissue, issuance withholding, retained old access, trusted-checkpoint rollback detection, payload-preserving DEK rewrap, both escrow paths and a measured ledger. It is not RW15 revocation, revocable ABE, revocable-storage ABE, self-updatable encryption or public ciphertext update. Exact-main run 40116671435 passed 226 unit tests, 36 learner-claim tests and three accessibility/reflow drives, then deployed assets matching a fresh build byte for byte.

### Beacon Lock

[`crypto-lab-beacon-lock`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-beacon-lock/) · Timelock Encryption · ENCRYPTION, RANDOMNESS

Lock a ciphertext to a future drand round and let the beacon's BLS signature be the decryption key — identity-based encryption with a clock in place of an authority.

    - **Limits:** Round progression is an in-tab clock, not drand network consensus.

    - **Limits:** Pairing and envelope encryption are real; beacon ticking is an in-page simulation with a known secret.

### Biham Lens

[`crypto-lab-biham-lens`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-biham-lens/) · Differential Cryptanalysis · ATTACKS

Differential cryptanalysis on a toy SPN and real FEAL-4: inspect difference tables, recover the toy last-round subkey, then verify equivalent FEAL round keys against fresh blocks without recovering its master key.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Differential Cryptanalysis, SPN, DDT, Chosen-Plaintext — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** PRESENT `src/crypto/present/present.ts:21`, Toy SPN `src/crypto/spn.ts:95`
- **Source review:** [8544ee0ff488](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-biham-lens/commit/8544ee0ff488f74ce437be57ac5cfd494bbe134c) — Re-read the complete prior-pin change inventory, SPN/FEAL source and added PRESENT-80 core, inverse schedule, analysis, worker and UI. The original toy SPN anchor remains; FEAL-4 and full-round PRESENT-80 are distinct engines. PRESENT recovery assumes known K32 and exhausts 16 missing register bits; it does not obtain K32 or break full PRESENT. The October 21 correction changes teaching prose and the DES comparison, not these engines. DES is reference context only; an independent FIPS-table test establishes its nonzero-input DDT maximum of 16/64, with a successful wrong-value mutation kill. No round count guarantees attack immunity. Remove chosen-ciphertext, collision and padding-oracle credits sourced only from Related Demos links, and linear-cryptanalysis credit sourced only from Serpent context; these attacks are not executed here.

### CKKS Lab

[`crypto-lab-ckks-lab`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-ckks-lab/) · Homomorphic Encryption · HOMOMORPHIC

Approximate FHE for encrypted floating-point arithmetic, homomorphic neural network inference, rescaling, and the complete FHE trilogy (TFHE + BGV/BFV + CKKS).

- **Card topics (discovery only):** CKKS, RLWE, Approximate FHE, Encrypted Inference — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** CKKS `src/toyCkks.ts:209`
- **Source review:** [e2f3e59a4c5a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-ckks-lab/commit/e2f3e59a4c5af667dab219c5c7048401dcd3f83b) — Read the complete symmetric CKKS teaching engine, UI, README, tests and visible limitations while reconciling CL123. The lab executes bounded encoding, symmetric encryption/decryption, addition, multiplication and rescaling, including gadget/digit evaluation-key key switching for relinearization. It does not implement public-key encryption, fresh public Enc(0), the Galois rotation/key-switching path needed for CoeffToSlot, CoeffToSlot itself, a separate client validity predicate or the paper's adaptive reaction attacker. Chosen-plaintext and key-recovery phrases describe the absent paper attack or limitations rather than an executed attack; the generic side-channel phrase likewise does not identify a separate runnable attack. Remove those three credits. This review does not claim a faithful reaction-attack reproduction or transfer the paper's asymptotic query complexity.

### Clock Arithmetic

[`crypto-lab-clock-arithmetic`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-clock-arithmetic/) · Arithmetic Before the Cipher · KEY EXCHANGE, ENCRYPTION

Step through exact BigInt arithmetic under RSA and finite-field Diffie–Hellman: inverses, Euler φ, orders, generators, subgroups and generalized CRT. Then encode, multiply and square through Montgomery REDC while exposing cancellation, radix shifts, final subtraction and bounded fixed-work timings.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Modular Arithmetic, Extended Euclid, Euler φ, CRT, Montgomery REDC — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Diffie-Hellman `src/nt/toyDh.ts:26`, Montgomery multiplication `src/nt/montgomery.ts:96`
- **Source review:** [e6e1e39b124c](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-clock-arithmetic/commit/e6e1e39b124c877fd17c5d9b0a3fa03a070dfd6e) — Read the complete merged README, source, tests, learner interface and visible limitations at this exact main commit. The existing exact BigInt lessons remain: signed modular wraparound, Euclidean/Bézout inverses, Euler phi by enumeration and factorization, multiplicative orders, generator and subgroup enumeration with toy finite-field Diffie–Hellman, and generalized CRT. The seventh exhibit implements the power-of-two Montgomery specialization for odd N at most 10^12 with a learner-supplied power-of-two R greater than N. Setup derives N′ = −N^-1 mod R and R² mod N; encoding executes REDC(x·R²), and multiplication retains T, its low radix word, m, mN, the divisible sum, the pre-subtraction candidate, the optional final subtraction and the reduced output. The N=9, R=16 fixture exposes candidate 9 before subtraction to 0. A product-square-times-a chain stays encoded until one final REDC and is checked against the ordinary canonical remainder. The fixed comparison executes the same 4,096-operation alternating multiply/square schedule on both routes and reports setup, ordinary loop, Montgomery loop and final decoding separately. The encoded loop performs this implementation’s validation and trace-object work on every operation, so the single Worker timings are not a benchmark, a speedup claim or evidence of constant-time behavior; JavaScript BigInt is not constant-time. Negative and oversized operands are normalized, while even or over-budget moduli and radices that are too small or not powers of two are refused. Montgomery multiplication is distinct from the Montgomery ladder. The bounded trial division and toy shared-secret enumeration support the arithmetic lesson rather than executing factoring, discrete-log, brute-force or man-in-the-middle attacks; software CRT faults and adjacent algorithms occur only in historical handoff prose or related links.
- **References:** AES, Baby-step giant-step, EC point arithmetic, ElGamal, Jacobi symbol, Miller–Rabin, Montgomery ladder, Pohlig–Hellman, RSA, SHA-256

### Collision Vault

[`crypto-lab-collision-vault`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-collision-vault/) · Hash Collisions · HASHING & KDFS, ATTACKS

Verify published MD5 and SHA-1 collision pairs, then compare full-round SHA-256 and SHA-3 digests. A separate research verifier checks a published 36-step SHA-256 pair.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** MD5, SHA-1, SHAttered, Chosen-Prefix Collision — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** MD5 `demos/collision-vault/src/hashing/md5.ts:10`, SHA-1 `demos/collision-vault/src/hashing/trace.ts:111`, SHA-256 `demos/collision-vault/src/hashing/index.ts:79`, SHA-3 `demos/collision-vault/src/hashing/sha3.ts:9`, SHA-512 `demos/collision-vault/src/hashing/index.ts:81`
- **Source review:** [9e4c26555dfe](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-collision-vault/commit/9e4c26555dfea4cd4b82bb6a07968495f7c9eb76) — Reviewed the published 12 October change, Table 2 fixture and complete Python verifier. Existing full-round providers and SHA-256/SHA-512 call-site anchors 79/81 remain unchanged. The isolated JavaScript research backend computes SHA-256 compression over big-endian blocks with the standard IV, explicit step count, per-block feed-forward and no added padding. The supplied two-block messages reproduce the 36-step Table 2 value from the 9 September 2026 preprint; this is distinct from its semi-free-start appendix examples. Normal WebCrypto SHA-256 with message padding produces different digests. Independent Python and TypeScript checks reproduce the result, reject all 1,024 one-bit mutations and distinguish incorrect round/IV/padding interpretations. Common padding preserves the reduced-round collision but changes the reported chaining value. The 64-step engine matches independent noble SHA-256 at padding boundaries. Local checks passed 118 units, lint/build and 35 browser tests, with one existing intentional skip; deployment passed separately. The sole Python file is the fully reviewed independent CI verifier, not an opaque browser component. The fixture records mirror retrieval and PDF fingerprint. This verifies a supplied pair, not its search cost, a full-round break, conformance certification or constant-time behavior.

### Credential Veil

[`crypto-lab-credential-veil`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-credential-veil/) · Anonymous Credentials · SIGNATURES, PRIVACY, ZERO-KNOWLEDGE

BBS selective disclosure over BLS12-381, checked against draft-13 vectors. Reveal chosen fields, compare presentation linkability, and explore a custom over-18 proof.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** BBS, Selective Disclosure, Unlinkability, Range Proof — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** BBS signatures `src/bbs/bbs.ts:151`, BLS12-381 `src/bbs/ciphersuite.ts:152`, Ed25519 `src/baseline/ed25519.ts:29`, Hash-to-curve `src/bbs/generators.ts:18`, Pairing `src/bbs/ciphersuite.ts:152`, Pedersen commitment `src/predicate/ageProof.ts:127`, SHA-256 `src/bbs/ciphersuite.ts:91`
- **Source review:** [963e6f6635b2](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-credential-veil/commit/963e6f6635b2bb1c4915bff53fa4ed296872aa82) — Reviewed the draft-13 baseline upgrade at this commit: numbered 13 October 2026 reference and publisher snapshot 104bdcd85869ac05d1c621e064222441404e019b. All 30 SHA-256 publisher fixture files are unchanged; remote reference/artifact hashes, 103 unit tests and production build passed. The core now rejects zero signed messages under section 4.2.3 while preserving empty-valued messages and no/some/all disclosure. Separate helper arguments and point sums implement the reviewed equations; the review documents this layout difference from draft-13. BBS proof-value unlinkability covers issuer/verifier coalitions, but identifying disclosures and context remain correlatable. Preserve the earlier source classification: implements CFRG draft BBS (A,e), not BBS+ or BLS signing; discrete-log assumptions and lack of side-channel review are risk prose, not executed attacks. The q-signature key-recovery paper is research context, not an attack this lab executes. Draft vectors do not validate the custom DOB/age-proof composition, production privacy, constant-time behavior or final-RFC status. Original source revision remains unknown in the historical note.
- **References:** Bulletproofs, EC point arithmetic, Private information retrieval, RSA, SHAKE, Schnorr, Schnorr identification, Shamir secret sharing, Sigma protocol
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST

  - **Age Predicate without Birth Date** (`age`; interactive; real-crypto)

### Curve Lens

[`crypto-lab-curve-lens`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-curve-lens/) · Elliptic Curves · KEY EXCHANGE

Point addition, scalar multiplication, and live ECDH across P-256, Curve25519, secp256k1, and brainpoolP256r1, whose RFC 5639 seeds it recomputes from π and e. Reconstruct P-256's seed from the timestamp-based recipe disclosed in October 2026, with the remaining provenance questions explained.

- **References:** AES, ChaCha20, Diffie-Hellman, Double Ratchet, ECDSA, Ed25519, Ed448, HKDF, Kuznyechik, ML-KEM, MLS, Montgomery ladder, PQXDH, RSA, Schnorr, Shor's algorithm, TLS 1.3, WebAuthn, X3DH, X448

- **Implementation:** @noble
- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [1ea00aa0c00f](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-curve-lens/commit/1ea00aa0c00f2d8e918413e8918faf6f97f7c65e) reviewed 2026-10-22; 5 mapped sections.
  - **Curve Explorer** (`panel1`; interactive; simulation)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 1 — Curve Explorer

    - **Observed result:** See the third intersection, reflection and resulting P+Q, with finite-field line segments wrapping modulo 17.

### DC-net

[`crypto-lab-dc-net`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-dc-net/) · Anonymous Broadcast · PRIVACY, PROTOCOLS

Cancel five participants’ pairwise XOR masks to reveal one anonymous public message, compare observer and coalition views, then execute collisions, jamming, dropout, commitment, reuse and later-disclosure failures.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** DC-net, Pairwise XOR, Coalition Views, Disruption — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** DC-net `src/dcnet/round.ts:171`, SHA-256 `src/dcnet/commitment.ts:148`
- **Source review:** [8de5cb25042c](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-dc-net/commit/8de5cb25042cc70b991fe53211d85e3324bc9684) — Read the complete merged README, security notes, implementation, tests and learner interface at this exact main commit. The five-participant cycle computes each one-byte broadcast from one input and every incident pairwise XOR mask, aggregates the public transcript, and independently exhausts small mask assignments for observer-view comparisons. Participant and coalition views remove exactly the masks they know, derive remaining connected components and component parities, and retain supplied priors when the explicit exactly-one-sender assumption is compatible. Separate executable cases cover zero through three senders, one-byte XOR collisions, malformed and correctly shaped dishonest contributions, current-round dropout, graph reformation with replacement masks, complete incident-mask reuse and later disclosure. The SHA-256 commit/reveal route is a bounded collect-all-then-reveal teaching adaptation: under collision and second-preimage resistance it binds the encoded context and contribution, while the nonce raises exhaustive-opening cost; it does not prove hiding, equation compliance, identity, availability, accountability or Dissent/Verdict properties. The anonymity result assumes the declared key graph, independent uniform secret one-use masks, synchrony and the stated observer knowledge; WebCrypto randomness is a concrete CSPRNG-backed execution, not proof of the information-theoretic theorem, and all roles share one browser origin. Hosted final-head and exact-main gates passed 44 unit tests, 11 learner-claim tests, 12 accessibility/reflow tests, zero audited dependency vulnerabilities and all 22 named mutations; exact-main CodeQL and Pages deployment passed, and the live HTML, JavaScript and CSS matched the reviewed build byte for byte.
- **References:** Shamir secret sharing
- **Attacks shown:** Known-plaintext attack `src/ui/app.ts:166`
- **Standards body:** NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto SHA-256 and random generation / local TypeScript DC-net and exhaustive finite observer models
- **Overlaps:** `crypto-lab-sphinx-mix` — Sphinx Mix constructs and peels layered packets across a mix path and separates packet-format unlinkability from traffic anonymity; DC-net cancels pairwise masks in one group broadcast and exposes collision, disruption and key-reuse limits.; `crypto-lab-blind-relay` — Blind Relay splits source identity and HTTP content across two non-colluding operators; DC-net instead derives sender ambiguity from a declared pairwise-key graph and observer knowledge.; `crypto-lab-silent-tally` — Silent Tally reconstructs a Shamir-shared aggregate without revealing individual counts; DC-net makes the XOR aggregate public while hiding which compatible participant supplied a lone message.

### Dedup Vault

[`crypto-lab-dedup-vault`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-dedup-vault/) · Encrypted Deduplication · ENCRYPTION, PRIVACY, ATTACKS

Compare fresh-key, local message-locked and server-aided encryption for equal files; measure deduplication and dictionary pressure, then separate possession, authorization, deletion, revocation and rotation.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Message-Locked Encryption, AES-CTR, AES-SIV, VOPRF — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/aes.ts:74`, AES-CTR `src/crypto/aes.ts:74`, AES-SIV `src/crypto/aes.ts:115`, Message-Locked Encryption `src/crypto/aes.ts:57`, OPRF `src/crypto/voprf.ts:208`, P-256 `src/crypto/voprf.ts:85`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/bytes.ts:72`
- **Source review:** [3cbf467bdb1a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-dedup-vault/commit/3cbf467bdb1a67cce39466e2e335e443530ac171) — Read the complete merged README, source, tests, learner interface and limits at this exact main commit. Two equal synthetic uploads execute fresh random AES-CTR keys, local first128(SHA-256(P || M)) message-locked derivation and RFC 9497 P256-SHA256 VOPRF derivation. Per-user RFC 5297 AES-SIV capsules bind scheme version, owner, reference and the complete data ciphertext; storage uses a digest only to select a bucket and deduplicates after full ciphertext-byte equality. The attack lesson computes local offline guesses, allowlisted per-principal/per-epoch online guesses, changed identities and epochs, proof tampering and key-server compromise. Separate executed cases distinguish bounded whole-ciphertext possession, reference authorization, last-reference deletion, prospective revocation with cached-copy limits and nonretroactive rotation. This is a DupLESS-shaped adaptation, not byte-for-byte DupLESS, a formal scalable proof-of-ownership protocol, process isolation, enforceable production rate limiting or a hardened storage service. Each derived AES-CTR key/counter pair is confined to one distinct plaintext value; repeats of that exact value intentionally reuse the pair and ciphertext. Hosted PR run 40055127586 passed 38 unit tests, 7 learner claims, 11 accessibility/reflow tests and all 24 named mutations; CodeQL run 40055127584 passed.
- **References:** CMAC, HMAC, OPAQUE, RSA
- **Attacks shown:** Dictionary attack `src/attacks/dictionary.ts:18`
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST

### DVD Scramble

[`crypto-lab-dvd-scramble`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-dvd-scramble/) · CSS Stream Cipher · ATTACKS, ENCRYPTION

Break the two-LFSR Content Scrambling System: guess the smaller register, let algebra fix the rest, enumerate 65,536 seeds against known bytes, then verify the key on 32 unseen ones.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** CSS, LFSR, Known-Plaintext, Key Recovery — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **Source review:** [f3d4bad6c5cf](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-dvd-scramble/commit/f3d4bad6c5cf660ebea5306460481099521d927d) — Source review of src/css/lfsr.ts, src/css/css.ts, src/attack/divide.ts and src/verify/verify.ts. lfsr.ts cites Boneh-Shoup v0.6 section 3.8 Figure 3.10 and computes a bit-serial LFSR: step() returns bit 0, XORs the declared taps, right-shifts and feeds back into the top bit; byte() clocks eight steps LSB- or MSB-first. css.ts generate() seeds a 17-bit register with taps [14,0] and a 25-bit register with taps [12,4,3,0], clocks a byte from each and adds them with carry, so z = (x+y+carry) mod 256 and the carry persists -- the CSS byte-serial combiner. The key space is 16 bits plus 24 bits, validated as such, which is the 40 bits the attack exhibit is about. divide.ts recover() enumerates smaller-register seeds and returns counted candidates; verify.ts checks a candidate against continuation bytes the search never saw. Zero runtime dependencies. N/A means no named algorithm IN THIS INDEX, not no computation: the Content Scrambling System and the LFSR family are outside the current vocabulary, the same reason crypto-lab-lfsr-forge was reviewed N/A on 2026-10-09. Scope recorded with it: this is the textbook generator, and the source says so in its own extension note -- deployed CSS changes insertion positions, discards early bytes and has inverter modes, none of which are implemented here. So the card must not be read as a deployed-CSS implementation.

### ElGamal Plain

[`crypto-lab-elgamal-plain`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-elgamal-plain/) · Public-Key Encryption · ENCRYPTION, HOMOMORPHIC

Taher ElGamal's 1985 scheme with fresh ephemeral randomness, multiplicative homomorphism, and ciphertext rerandomization across toy and RFC 3526 groups.

Read README Security Lab, src/attacks.ts, src/groups.ts, modular exponentiation/inverse helpers and src/attacks.test.ts. discreteLog builds g^j baby steps, then searches target times g^(-m*i) with m=ceil(sqrt(q)); the q guard refuses RFC 3526 Group 14. This is executable toy-group key recovery, not a reference-only mention. Its algorithm name appears only in comments, so add the implementation at the exported function through this reviewed supplement rather than reading comments as implementations globally. The attack implementation and tests are unchanged from the historical 72048d72 interpretation; the full 15-path change inventory was compared, and the solver and its tests remain byte-identical. The newer Cramer-Shoup exhibit is outside this bounded solver review. Actual current npm test passes 127 tests, including 300 toy-key recoveries, operation-count and large-group refusal controls. This review only adds the bounded solver credit; it does not claim constant-time execution, real-group key recovery, or full cryptographic conformance. ### Envelope KMS

[`crypto-lab-envelope-kms`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-envelope-kms/) · Envelope Encryption · ENCRYPTION, KEY EXCHANGE, PROTOCOLS

Explore RFC 3394/5649 AES key wrap, DEK/KEK rotation, AES-GCM context binding, and caller authorization before unwrap. Search a bounded key-handle model for disclosure witnesses, then replay found traces with real AES-KW and verify recovered material with AES-GCM. Compare static and key-evolving HMAC audit logs under logger compromise, suffix forgery, truncation, checkpoints, and external freshness evidence.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** RFC 3394, AES Key Wrap, DEK/KEK, Key Rotation, HMAC-SHA-256 — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/aead.ts:9`, AES-CTR `src/security/properties.ts:90`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/aead.ts:9`, AES-KW `src/crypto/aes-kw.ts:78`, HKDF `src/crypto/kdf.ts:1`, HMAC `src/kms/forward-secure-log.ts:220`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/kdf.ts:1`
- **Source review:** [d2b6614a9fad](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-envelope-kms/commit/d2b6614a9fad2fe9667b05d35e3a1e6895ad3293) — Reviewed the complete E-K-01 key-handle and S02 key-evolving audit-log source, interfaces, tests, browser claims, security notes and change inventory at exact merged main. Existing AES, AES-CTR, AES-GCM, AES-KW, HKDF and SHA-256 implementation anchors are unchanged; S02 adds a direct HMAC-SHA-256 implementation anchor. The key-handle exercises retain real RFC 3394 replay, independent AES-GCM verification, three declared finite presets, bounded no-witness versus incomplete-cutoff reporting and the non-PKCS #11/non-HSM boundary. The new integrity-only lesson compares a static HMAC key with a domain-separated evolving state, models compromise immediately before period c, rejects an earlier evolving-key rewrite under the one-way-evolution and erasure assumptions, and shows that both tracks can forge from c onward. Retained checkpoint, expected CLOSE and outside-heartbeat inputs produce separate integrity, consistency, completeness and freshness results. Exact-main run 40166747041 passed 154 unit tests, 2 publishing controls, 49 browser/accessibility/reflow tests, zero dependency vulnerabilities and all 18 combined mutations; CodeQL run 40166747021 passed. Remove Fault injection because source mutation verifies tests rather than executing a cryptographic fault attack; remove Side-channel (unspecified) because the briefs exclude that claim. The S02 construction is a bounded single-logger/private-verifier adaptation, not the full Schneier–Kelsey protocol, Bellare–Yee's exact construction, a standardized wire format or a security proof; JavaScript cannot guarantee erasure, messages remain plaintext and key evolution or a linear checkpoint alone does not establish completeness, freshness, availability, global consistency or split-view resistance. Merge, deployment and byte-matched live evidence are recorded separately in the implementation roadmap.
- **References:** Argon2, FF1, Merkle tree, PBKDF2, RSA, scrypt
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto

### Factor Forge

[`crypto-lab-factor-forge`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-factor-forge/) · Integer Factorization · ENCRYPTION, ATTACKS

Seven classical factoring methods on a real BigInt N, each waiting for a different mistake in key generation. Obey every RSA rule and rho and ECM still finish; only size stops them.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Pollard Rho, Lenstra ECM, Quadratic Sieve, Fermat — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Jacobi symbol `src/factor/bigint.ts:139`, Miller–Rabin `src/factor/primality.ts:52`, Shor's algorithm `src/ui/shor.ts:98`
- **Source review:** [5849f2d4b424](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-factor-forge/commit/5849f2d4b42432f25b769b8bc02916582c7f1905) — Bounded current-source review of the Brute force credit only. README.md:223 (formerly :210 before a thirteen-line documentation insertion) describes a Jacobi unit-test reference oracle; src/factor/bigint.test.ts:76-85 enumerates quadratic residues for five small primes to check jacobi. This is test support, not an attack exhibit, so exclude that README-derived Brute force credit. The actual trial-division implementation and its registry/worker wiring were inspected and remain unchanged. ### Function Key

[`crypto-lab-function-key`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-function-key/) · Functional Encryption · ENCRYPTION

Issue a key that answers one question about an encrypted vector — its weighted sum — and nothing else. Then issue keys one at a time and watch the set of possible plaintexts shrink, until one more key hands over the master secret.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** ABDP15 IPFE, ristretto255, Baby-Step Giant-Step, Key Collusion — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** ABDP15 IPFE `src/crypto/attacks.ts:24`, Baby-step giant-step `src/crypto/dlog.ts:130`, EC point arithmetic `src/crypto/ristretto.ts:80`, ristretto255 `src/crypto/dlog.ts:25`, SHA-512 `src/crypto/prng.ts:47`
- **Source review:** [b145a348de07](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-function-key/commit/b145a348de0771eed22923c1da210c60e961bbf6) — Browser TypeScript throughout, no other language and no WASM. Group operations are @noble/curves 2.4.0, pinned to RFC 9496 Appendix A (16 A.1 multiples both directions, 29 A.2 rejections, 8 A.3 map outputs) before any scheme code was written on it; ABDP15 Construction 3.1 and the baby-step giant-step, exact-rational and mod-l algebra are implemented in-repo. Five derived attacks are removed because none is an attack this lab shows, and each was matched by a different accident: Man-in-the-middle came from the string 'DH MITM' inside CATALOG-ENTRY.md, which is this catalog's own concept line quoted back in the lab's handoff doc and not lab source at all; Signature malleability from /malleab/i on a seed label, in a lab that has no signatures - what it demonstrates is CIPHERTEXT malleability, and its own source calls that 'not an attack and not a flaw in the proof'; Chosen-plaintext attack from CPA inside 'IND-FE-CPA', the security notion ABDP15 proves rather than an attack mounted; Chosen-ciphertext attack from CCA inside 'Any CCA security whatever', a line in the NOT-BUILT list; and Discrete log from 'baby step', which this lab pays as a decryption cost and never mounts. The two attacks it does show, key collusion and ciphertext malleability, have no term in the vocabulary. Baby-step giant-step is added by review: src/crypto/dlog.ts is a baby-step giant-step over a symmetric range, but it names the algorithm only in comments and in the local counters babySteps and giantSteps, and the exported function is called dlogSymmetric. The anchor is that function, not the counter a narrower shape used to read. Re-reviewed at b145a348de0771eed22923c1da210c60e961bbf6 on 2026-10-09: compared the prior pin to current source; the only implementation change preserves disclosures and focused summaries during worker-driven redraws in src/main.ts. Read the current README, IPFE setup/key derivation/encryption/decryption and symmetric bounded BSGS. The cryptographic implementation, selective IND-FE-CPA/DDH scope, no-integrity limitation, reviewed additions and five exclusions remain unchanged. Current lab tests and deployed resource identity are recorded separately in the fleet evidence.

### Good Randomness

[`crypto-lab-good-randomness`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-good-randomness/) · Randomness Basics · RANDOMNESS

Two 32-byte keys pass the same look-random checks &mdash; one from the browser&rsquo;s generator, one from a ChaCha20 stream started at a four-digit PIN. Then the second is rebuilt by counting to ten thousand, while every check still reports success.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** ChaCha20, CSPRNG, Seed Recovery, WebCrypto — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/cipher.ts:29`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/cipher.ts:38`, ChaCha20 `src/crypto/chacha20.ts:86`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/seeded.ts:66`
- **Source review:** [f995c87c1fe0](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-good-randomness/commit/f995c87c1fe074dc57ee61b44c4c6df47a03de58) — Read src/crypto/chacha20.ts, cipher.ts, pinned.ts and vectors.ts. ChaCha20 is HAND-ROLLED here rather than imported, because it is the teaching subject and a reader has to be able to open the file: the scanner anchored it at src/crypto/pinned.ts:18, which is that file's import line, so the pin moves it to the block function it actually implements. AES-GCM and SHA-256 come from crypto.subtle and their anchors are the real call sites. The lab's point is that a generator seeded from a guessable value produces guessable keys while every check on the page still reports success -- the key from a four-digit PIN is rebuilt by trying ten thousand seeds, which is counting rather than cryptanalysis.

- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto

### Hash Hunt

[`crypto-lab-hash-hunt`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-hash-hunt/) · Generic Hash Attacks · HASHING &amp; KDFS, ATTACKS

Find shortened-hash collisions, test an insecure hash-then-MAC composition, and measure chain and salt tradeoffs. Compare attacker-chosen public hash-table buckets with a secret keyed map.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Truncated SHA-256, Floyd Cycle Finding, Hellman / Rainbow Chains, HMAC-SHA-256, Hash-Table Flood — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Floyd cycle finding `src/attack/floyd.ts:2`, Hellman chains `src/attack/tmto/tables.ts:8`, HMAC `src/mac/hashAndMac.ts:2`, Rainbow chains `src/attack/tmto/tables.ts:8`, SHA-256 `src/hash/truncate.ts:3`
- **Source review:** [072a9531796a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-hash-hunt/commit/072a9531796a1c2f9936197077aee2ee0d57b144) — Reviewed the existing shortened-SHA-256 collision, meaningful-letter HMAC composition, chain and salt exhibits plus the new bounded table-flood panel. It searches distinct names that hit one public FNV-1a bucket, counts linear-probing slot visits, then reuses the same names with fresh secret WebCrypto HMAC-SHA-256 buckets. It does not implement SipHash or measure a real server. The separate tag transfer attacks a deliberately collision-prone hash-then-MAC composition, not HMAC or full SHA-256; Hellman/rainbow and salt limits remain. Unit, browser and mutation gates passed on the lab main build.
- **References:** Grover's algorithm, MD5, Merkle tree, SHA-1, bcrypt
- **Attacks shown:** Birthday bound `brief-extension.md:61`, Collision attack `README.md:14`, Hash-flooding `src/main.ts:2`

- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [072a9531796a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-hash-hunt/commit/072a9531796a1c2f9936197077aee2ee0d57b144) reviewed 2026-10-23; 7 mapped sections.

    - **Visible section:** Build exponentially many messages from a linear chain of forks
    - **Learner action:** Build b forks in a toy iterated hash, enumerate or flip combinations, and search H1‖H2.
    - **Observed result:** A linear number of small collision searches yields exponentially many H1-equivalent messages and can weaken naive concatenation.
    - **Concepts taught:** Joux multicollision; Merkle–Damgård; hash concatenation; length strengthening
    - **Limits:** The compression output is deliberately tiny; this does not attack full SHA-256 or contradict Merkle–Damgård collision-preservation results.

  - **Salted Target Experiment** (`salt`; interactive; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Precompute first. Learn the salt afterward.
    - **Learner action:** Precompute an unsalted table, draw fresh per-user salts, then test old candidates and guess each salted target.
    - **Observed result:** Old table hits mostly fail salted verification while per-user guessing still recovers valid preimages.
    - **Concepts taught:** salt; precomputation resistance; per-target guessing; preimage versus original password
    - **Limits:** With a 12-bit digest, accidental matches and multiple preimages are common; recovery of a preimage does not identify the original password.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:33`, `src/salt/experiment.ts:1`
  - **Unkeyed versus secret-key hash-table buckets** (`table-flood`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** When the hash table becomes the target
    - **Learner action:** Search attacker-chosen names for one exposed bucket, insert them with linear probing, then reuse the same names under a fresh secret HMAC-SHA-256 bucket map.
    - **Observed result:** Compare measured slot visits and per-insertion probes for public versus keyed starting buckets in the same small table.
    - **Concepts taught:** hash-table flooding; chosen input; keyed hashing; linear probing; hash denial-of-service
    - **Limits:** The public mapping is a deliberately weak FNV-1a bucket index and the keyed comparator uses WebCrypto HMAC, not SipHash. Slot visits in this toy are not a SHA-256 collision, a server benchmark, or a proven denial-of-service exploit.

The original RFC 9180 pipeline, all four modes, context-binding failures, replay and non-goals remain. The S01 comparison now executes the RFC 9180 Auth recipient-key KCI forgery with recipient skR and public sender pkS, without sender skS. Its separate versioned multi-user Sign-then-Encrypt profile signs sender, recipient, independently expected application context and message with strict Ed25519, then encrypts the framed signed payload with Base HPKE; pinned identity-to-key records are external to the packet. Executed cases cover outsider tampering, recipient/sender/both-key compromise, recipient forwarding, public signature evidence and replay. Application plaintext and evidence remain quarantined until signature and all identity/context bindings pass. The profile is an An-Dodis-Rabin-style teaching instantiation, not a standardized wire format, production protocol or automatic transfer of the paper's proof. Public evidence establishes only that the separately pinned signing key signed the exact disclosed fields; it does not prove ciphertext authorship, transmission, receipt, time, human intent or legal non-repudiation. The phrase Apple iCloud key recovery names a provider feature, and the nonce-collision URL is a related-lab link; neither is an attack executed here, so both old scanner credits are removed. Exact-main run 40179028196 passed 258 unit tests, all 19 clean-baseline mutations, the production build and all 27 hosted browser/accessibility tests, deployed, and the served HTML, JavaScript and CSS matched the exact reviewed tree byte for byte.

### HTTPS Padlock

[`crypto-lab-https-padlock`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-https-padlock/) · What the Padlock Means · PROTOCOLS, SIGNATURES

Takes apart a certificate a real site presented, lets you break each of its four checks in turn, then shows a flawless certificate for a lookalike domain that passes every one. Reads captured certificates; it never connects to a site.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X.509, ECDSA P-256, RFC 5280 Subset, ClientHello Bytes Only — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **Source review:** [f5d5b09b548b](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-https-padlock/commit/f5d5b09b548bcb2f67b133bd19044cc3fc577eaa) — Read src/pki/path.ts, parse.ts, assess.ts, break.ts and src/tls/clienthello.ts. The scanner found only X25519 in the ClientHello builder. The chain walk really does verify every signature: src/pki/path.ts:86 calls @peculiar/x509's verify with the parent's public key and the WebCrypto provider, over real DER TBS bytes, and the certificates this lab ships are ECDSA over P-256 and P-384 -- so ECDSA is pinned above. Scope that the card and chips are written to respect: the lab makes NO network connection and runs no handshake, so it never observes encryption; it reads certificates captured earlier. Its RFC 5280 path validation is a stated teaching subset, deliberately omitting revocation, name constraints, policy constraints and path length, so a chain this page accepts is not thereby a chain a browser would accept. The ClientHello is encoded byte for byte and never sent, and its X25519 private half is discarded unused -- which is why the chip is marked 'ClientHello Bytes Only' rather than claiming TLS 1.3. Trust terminates in the lab's own committed copy of a root list, not the reader's device trust store, and the page says so. Re-read current hostname.ts, original PKI path and ClientHello at this exact SHA after PR4/5. Authority ends before path/query/fragment userinfo; 68 unit, 63 verdict, 3 full-state accessibility checks and 24 live URL/SNI/reflow controls verify the bounded repair. ECDSA anchor and captured-certificate/offline/partial-validation limitations remain unchanged; this review does not assert a live TLS handshake. Re-read complete current path.ts and parse.ts, bounded assess/ClientHello callers, trust-anchor regression controls and PR7 at f5d5b09. Actual held subject/SPKI identity now terminates cross-signed paths; copied subject with a different key rejects, genuine same-key cross-signs remain valid and held/served date policy stays explicit. X5092 reflection initialization preserves real ECDSA verification. Existing ECDSA86/X25519 ClientHello282 anchors unchanged. This source review retains offline captured-certificate/partial RFC5280 limits and does not establish live TLS, full validation, revocation or constant-time behavior.

### Hybrid Sign

[`crypto-lab-hybrid-sign`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-hybrid-sign/) · Composite Signatures · POST-QUANTUM, SIGNATURES

Ed25519 plus ML-DSA-65 hybrid signatures per the IETF LAMPS composite-signature draft, framed as defense in depth for long-lived authenticity.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Ed25519, ML-DSA-65, Composite Signatures, IETF LAMPS — labels do not establish what any section runs.

The lab executes Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 signing and AND-gated verification through a local LAMPS draft-16 composite combiner. Its break scenarios grant the honest signing key for a modeled broken component; they do not execute Shor's algorithm, discrete-log, factoring, lattice or side-channel attacks. The word pairing describes combining the two signatures and is not a bilinear-pairing reference. The TLS working-group draft-00 and IANA registry were checked on 2026-10-24: mldsa65_ed25519_sha512 still uses placeholder TBD7, no SignatureScheme value is assigned, and the TLS draft references LAMPS draft-19. The lab remains explicitly pinned to its older draft-16 construction and implements no TLS negotiation, X.509 or CMS encoding, draft-19 construction, real cryptanalysis or hardened production signing. Exact-main run 40092067603 passed 19 unit tests, the production build and 11 hosted browser/accessibility tests before deploying byte-matching public assets.

### Key Mirror

[`crypto-lab-key-mirror`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-key-mirror/) · Key Transparency · PROTOCOLS, HASHING & KDFS

The scope panel explicitly lists the length-extension attack itself as deliberately not built and links to Mac Race and Babel Hash; it is a contrast to the sponge/KMAC mechanisms, not an executed attack in this lab. Remove that prose-derived attack credit. Preserve actual computations and sibling links. ### LFSR Forge

[`crypto-lab-lfsr-forge`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-lfsr-forge/) · Fit, Forecast, Then Verify · ENCRYPTION, RANDOMNESS, ATTACKS, HISTORICAL

Fit and verify LFSR recurrences, recover tiny Geffe states, inspect real Trivium clocking, audit editable Boolean combiners, execute toy-oracle cube sums that recover affine superpolys, and trace reverse-engineered historical A5/1 majority clocking with a bounded leaked-state completion.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** LFSR, Berlekamp–Massey, Geffe Generator, Trivium, Boolean Function Audit, Cube Sums, Superpolys, Historical A5/1, Majority Clocking — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** A5/1 `src/a51/a51.ts:125`, Trivium `src/trivium/trivium.ts:29`
- **Source review:** [c4ef2da4b33f](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-lfsr-forge/commit/c4ef2da4b33fd08382a4309d9665745cb30bbda5) — Read the complete merged README, source, tests, learner interface and visible limitations at this exact main commit. The existing binary Fibonacci LFSR, Berlekamp-Massey, Geffe-correlation and eSTREAM-vector-checked Trivium lessons remain, and the Trivium implementation anchors directly at the state-advance function rather than at a panel mount. The zero-round recovery builds 66 public equations over 80 key bits, exhausts the remaining 14-bit space, rechecks every candidate against the complete 1,024-bit observation and compares a unique candidate with the hidden key separately; the specified 1,152-round route rejects this model, and the lesson does not claim a cube attack against full Trivium. The Boolean panel exhaustively analyzes an editable four-input truth table: exact ANF and degree, all 16 Walsh coefficients, balance, nonlinearity, every fixed-subset distribution, correlation immunity, resiliency and 4,094 candidate-side checks over all 2,047 nonzero degree-at-most-two polynomials. Its deterministic counterexamples fit parity with Berlekamp-Massey, scan all 105 R1/R2 state pairs against an order-one-resilient function and scan all 127 R4 states against an algebraic-immunity-two function; worker inputs contain only copied output and the fixed public profile, while hidden-state comparisons stay in the controller. The eighth panel executes a cube attack on its own explicit three-secret/four-public degree-four GF(2) toy oracle. Preprocessing exhausts four two-variable cube faces over all eight teaching keys, computes 128 raw evaluations covering 72 distinct secret/public-row pairs and derives each superpoly by Möbius transform. C12, C13 and C24 are affine maxterms whose rank-three system filters 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 to key 110 from sums 111; C34 is a valid cube with the quadratic superpoly k1k2 ⊕ k3, is not a maxterm, and is excluded only from this bounded affine solve. The candidate is frozen before four disjoint held-out public rows; their 1011 fingerprint is injective over the eight teaching keys and precedes a separate controller comparison. Dropping C24 leaves 001 and 110, while flipping C13 recovers wrong candidate 000 before held-outs reject it. Online work is 12 raw cube-vertex evaluations plus four held-outs, 16 raw evaluations across 12 distinct public rows. The panel executes no Trivium state or round and makes no attack or cost claim against full Trivium; the cited paper treats only 672-, 735- and 767-round reduced variants. Its source-visible publication caveat says direct evaluation of ePrint 2008/385's printed introductory polynomial adds a constant 1 to the stated v3 = 0 face sum, so the lab uses its own independently checkable oracle and does not call that an official erratum. The ninth panel implements the reverse-engineered historical BGW A5/1 definition, not a public modern standard: distinct 19/22/23-bit registers, least-significant-bit-first Kc and COUNT loading, 100 output-disabled majority clocks and clock-before-output generation. Independently transcribed setup code derives the post-key, post-COUNT and post-100 checkpoint states, then matches the two published consecutive 114-bit bursts. Its separate bounded adaptation discloses an extraordinary 52 exact bits of one post-100 state, enumerates the remaining 4,096 completions and filters candidate 1425 with 32 aligned known-keystream bits before 32 disjoint held-out bits and a separate controller-state comparison. Sixteen bits leave 11 candidates, regular clocking leaves none after two observations, and flipping observation 29 selects wrong candidate 1409 before 11 held-out mismatches reject it. The worker receives only the masked 52-bit disclosure, copied observations, clock model and run identifier; it receives no full hidden state or Kc. The exercise is not a published A5/1 attack, does not recover Kc and does not model modern cellular encryption. The merged gates cover 47 unit tests, 23 browser tests, all nine panels at desktop/380px plus the 320px extension, and 33 clean-baseline mutations. Walsh probabilities and fixed-subset independence assume independent uniform table inputs; LFSR agreement is measured separately, both state scans are bounded toy searches, nonlinear-superpoly techniques remain out of scope, and algebraic immunity does not exclude every fast algebraic relation. The literal Brute force scanner hit appears only in the independent unit-test oracle. Panel 09 separately exhausts 2^12 state completions under disclosure of 52 exact post-100 state bits; the catalog records that narrowly as bounded state completion, not as a generic brute-force attack or A5/1/Kc attack. Known plaintext/ciphertext remains prose explaining how an external XOR-stream setting could reveal the already-supplied keystream and is not an attack workflow executed by this lab. Shamir names a cube-attack coauthor, while Pairing and RC4 are stale or lexical false references, so none of those three belongs in the algorithm reference list. BCH, ChaCha20, SHA-256, SNOW 3G and ZUC remain comparison or evidence context rather than implemented primitives.

### Locks and Keys

[`crypto-lab-locks-and-keys`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-locks-and-keys/) · Public-Key Basics · ENCRYPTION, SIGNATURES

Generate a public key and a separate, mathematically related private key. Encrypt and open a note with RSA-OAEP, then sign and verify with RSA-PSS. Try the wrong key and a changed message. No maths needed.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** RSA-OAEP, RSA-PSS, Public-Key Encryption, WebCrypto — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** RSA `src/crypto/lock.ts:40`, RSA-OAEP `src/crypto/pinned.ts:42`, RSA-PSS `src/crypto/pinned.ts:57`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/pair.ts:35`
- **Source review:** [cfdda6915fcf](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-locks-and-keys/commit/cfdda6915fcf9230d07b06da4f214525ce7dfd00) — Read src/crypto/pair.ts, lock.ts, sign.ts, vectors.ts, pinned.ts and vectors.test.ts. One 2048-bit RSA pair does two different jobs: RSAES-OAEP encryption and RSASSA-PSS signing. The page is careful that signing is NOT encryption run backwards, and the scanner's RSA / RSA-OAEP / RSA-PSS / SHA-256 anchors are the real WebCrypto call sites. Two negative claims are carried in the lab rather than implied: a successful decryption establishes nothing about WHO encrypted the message, since anyone holding the public key could have; and a verifying signature ties a note to a KEY, not to a person. Correctness rests on 12 pinned Project Wycheproof cases -- 6 OAEP and 6 PSS, of which 4 must be REFUSED -- taken from rsa_oaep_2048_sha256_mgf1sha256_test.json and rsa_pss_2048_sha256_mgf1_32_test.json and run in the reader's own browser. RFC 8017 is cited for the SCHEMES only (§7.1 RSAES-OAEP, §8.1 RSASSA-PSS) and never for the numbers, because RFC 8017 publishes no test data; src/crypto/vectors.test.ts asserts that attribution cannot drift. The build brief's claim of 'a pinned RSA-OAEP / RSA-PSS vector from RFC 8017's test data' was wrong and is corrected in audits/BRIEF-locks-and-keys.md. Re-read the 17 October copy changes and unchanged WebCrypto call sites: the page now explicitly says two separate mathematically related keys and trims repeated instructions. Encryption/signing behavior and published fixtures are unchanged.
- **References:** Ed25519, HPKE, ML-KEM, P-256, Schnorr, TLS 1.3
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto

[`crypto-lab-log-forge`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-log-forge/) · Discrete Logarithms · KEY EXCHANGE, ATTACKS

Generic solvers cannot import field/curve implementations. Every candidate is rechecked by an independent exponent or curve verifier. Large-order cases report partial information or budget exhaustion. [`crypto-lab-lwe-hints`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-lwe-hints/) · Lattice Cryptanalysis · ATTACKS, POST-QUANTUM

Counts how many leakage hints collapse an LWE lattice problem on sparse ternary secrets, then recovers a toy secret from real hints and tests the Gaussian assumption against sampled data. ePrint 2026/1081.

CPA in index.html:592 is paired with DPA under Power analysis: it means correlation power analysis, not a chosen-plaintext attack. The lab generates toy LWE samples and recovers a sparse ternary secret from perfect inner-product hints with adaptive group testing and finite-field linear algebra. Lattice reduction is the referenced paper method, explicitly not run here; power capture is a discussed channel and illustrative arithmetic preset, not a measured or simulated power-analysis experiment. Remove those three attack credits; preserve the real LWE implementation and generic assumed side-channel hint setting. The physical channel is assumed, not implemented. ### Matsui Line

[`crypto-lab-matsui-line`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-matsui-line/) · Linear Cryptanalysis · ATTACKS

Run linear analysis on a toy SPN: compare trails with key-dependent hulls, count two masks and a structural zero, then measure repeated versus distinct known plaintexts.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Linear Cryptanalysis, LAT, Piling-Up Lemma, Known-Plaintext, Multiple Masks — labels do not establish what any section runs.

It counts two parity relations and all four joint outcomes on the same 16/64/256 plaintexts, and checks a no-nonzero-trail pair whose full-codebook correlation is zero across keys. This is a bounded toy-SPN observation, not a multidimensional key-recovery attack or a reproduction of the cited ChaCha research. Existing single-trail versus full linear-hull and repeated versus distinct plaintext comparisons remain separate. The toy SPN implementation anchor is unchanged; no full DES or production cipher is attacked.

### McEliece Gate

[`crypto-lab-mceliece-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/) · Post-Quantum KEM · POST-QUANTUM

Run a toy binary Goppa code and Patterson decoder, then visualize Classic McEliece’s 261,120-byte public key using simulated bytes. McEliece began as public-key encryption in 1978; the later KEM was not selected when NIST chose HQC in 2025.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Toy Goppa Code, Simulated Key Sizes, Post-Quantum — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/mceliece.ts:173`, AES-GCM `src/mceliece.ts:182`, SHA-256 `src/mceliece.ts:81`
- **Source review:** [3f4a0d6ad769](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/commit/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25) — Reviewed src/mceliece.ts, src/toy/goppa-code.ts, keysize and comparison modules, visible UI, README, LIMITATIONS and tests at this pin. The browser computes a genuine small GF(16) Goppa/Patterson teaching model and a toy brute-force syndrome decoder. Its published-size 261120-byte key visual is SHA-256-expanded simulated bytes, not a Classic McEliece public key; its encapsulation is not the submitted KEM API. Real WebCrypto AES-GCM protects the teaching message. Classic McEliece is a referenced later KEM, not an implemented primitive here. The 2026 structural key-recovery preprint and possible public-key-substitution MitM are research/deployment context, not attacks executed by this lab. Preserve actual toy brute force and real AES/SHA operations while excluding full Classic McEliece, key recovery and MitM implementation credits. The 1978 scheme was public-key encryption; CRYSTALS-Kyber was selected in 2022 and standardized as ML-KEM in 2024. NIST selected HQC rather than Classic McEliece in 2025.
- **References:** BIKE, Classic McEliece, Grover's algorithm, HQC, Information-set decoding, Isogeny walk, Kyber, LWE, ML-KEM, NTRU, RSA, Reed-Muller, Reed-Solomon
- **Attacks shown:** Brute force `src/toy/goppa-code.ts:347`

### Power Trace

[`crypto-lab-power-trace`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-power-trace/) · Power Side-Channel · ATTACKS

Recover an AES-128 key byte from simulated power traces. Correlation and differential power analysis use real statistics on modeled leakage; the JavaScript AES is not constant-time. An idealized AES table cache-line observation leaves 16 candidates without measuring browser hardware leakage.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** CPA, DPA, AES-128, Hamming Weight — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **Source review:** [c8635e31bbc5](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-power-trace/commit/c8635e31bbc5ec93f0617a3bf5ee3747a08c70f1) — Re-read AES core, CPA/DPA code, leakage traces, Exhibit 8 cache model, UI, README and tests through this exact pin while reconciling CL092 and RR-POWER-MEASURED. CPA means correlation power analysis, not chosen-plaintext attack. Real AES block encryption is anchored at src/aes/aes.ts:123; browser power traces use its S-box intermediate, independently ranks all 256 guesses and verifies bounded byte recovery against retained ground truth, while the shipped JavaScript AES is not constant-time. The separate, idealized T-table exhibit uses a known plaintext byte and one 64-byte cache-line address observation to leave 16 possible key bytes versus 256 in an all-lines control. It neither measures browser cache timing nor recovers a full key. Fault injection is sibling context. Keep power analysis and bounded key-recovery credits; exclude chosen-plaintext, cache-timing, fault-injection, generic side-channel and timing-side-channel claims as separate executed attacks. NTT appears only in a related-demo link, and Shamir is the surname of a historical SPA coauthor rather than secret sharing, so remove both references. The present CPA/DPA path is not a profiled classifier; CL092 contributes future prior-aware measured-data controls, not a deep-learning claim.

### PQXDH Wire

[`crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/) · Post-Quantum Key Agreement · KEY EXCHANGE, POST-QUANTUM

One ML-KEM secret added to the X3DH transcript is what survives a future curve break. The prekey signature and the ratchet after it are untouched, so Bob can still be impersonated with every check green.

    - **Visible section:** Open the boxes the model grants

    - **Observed result:** With only the curve grant, it recomputes four DH outputs but lacks the KEM secret and cannot rederive the session key; with both grants, it derives the same session key.

### Prime Witness

[`crypto-lab-prime-witness`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-prime-witness/) · Primality Testing · RANDOMNESS, ATTACKS

Count Miller–Rabin lying bases, test fixed-base lists, and measure probable-prime generation. Then build and independently check a recursive proof for a small prime.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Miller–Rabin, Fermat Test, Prime Certificates, Prime Generation — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Fermat primality test `src/primality/fermat.ts:2`, Miller–Rabin `src/primality/millerRabin.ts:11`

Trial division creates factor proofs only for p ≤ 1,000,000; the verifier checks the complete factorization of p−1, recursive primality proofs and full-order modular witness without calling the generator. Separate Miller–Rabin outputs remain probable for large candidates; the FIPS 186-5 Table B.1 path is a limited generation-shape experiment, not conformant RSA generation or a DRBG. Trial factorization supports Korselt classification and the small proof generator, not a general factoring attack. Unit and browser checks are lab-specific and do not constitute machine verification or production security.

- **Standards body:** —

### Proof Tally

[`crypto-lab-proof-tally`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-proof-tally/) · Verifiable Aggregation · MPC & THRESHOLD, PRIVACY, ZERO-KNOWLEDGE

Prio3 lets two aggregators reject a malformed report without reading it. Separate lessons compare exact-total differencing with one bounded participant-noised release, then compute exact observable transcripts for selective aborts, conditioned publication, capped retries, and an independent-abort control.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Prio3, Fully Linear PCP, Field64, Discrete Laplace, Abort / Retry — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Laplace mechanism `src/distributed/noise.ts:95`, NTT `src/field/field64.ts:95`, SHA-3 `src/xof/turboshake.ts:1`, SHAKE `src/xof/turboshake.ts:33`
- **Source review:** [9394e3fd3fd8](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-proof-tally/commit/9394e3fd3fd84cab5cfa95016f21808ca9f4e395) — Re-read the current Field64 arithmetic and transforms, BBCGGI19-style FLP circuits, Prio3 report preparation/verification/aggregation, TurboSHAKE128 XOF wrapper, S04 distributed report/release path, exact CL084 abort/retry model, learner UI, tests, mutation records and README through this exact pin. The lab executes a local two-aggregator Prio3Count/Prio3Sum teaching implementation; @noble supplies TurboSHAKE128 only, not Prio3 or field/proof logic. The separate abort lesson uses reduced BigInt rational arithmetic over a finite additive-noise model with neighboring answers zero and one; it computes ordinary, selective-abort, conditioned-publication, capped fresh-retry and independent-abort transcripts without modifying or attacking the Prio3 route. Public, aborter-only and omniscient teaching views remain distinct. The S04 claim still assumes authenticated roster bindings, non-collusion, honest independent noise contributors, complete delivery and one accounted release, while the browser supplies no DAP transport, durable atomic ledger, production attestation or constant-time assurance. The CL084 adaptation does not establish the paper's general bounds or imply that every abort violates differential privacy.

### Regex Veil — FTE

[`crypto-lab-fte`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-fte/) · Format-Transforming Encryption · STEGANOGRAPHY, ENCRYPTION

Compiles a regex to a minimal DFA, counts its length-n language exactly, and enciphers real AES-CTR bytes into that slice with FF1 — output a DPI rule accepts, plus the substitution attack proving nothing is authenticated.

### Rekey Relay

[`crypto-lab-rekey-relay`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-rekey-relay/) · Proxy Re-Encryption · ENCRYPTION

A semi-trusted relay turns Alice's ciphertext into Bob's without ever holding the plaintext. In BBS98, the scheme everyone starts with, the relay and Bob recover Alice's private key in one modular division.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** BBS98, AFGH, BLS12-381, Re-Encryption Key — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/kem.ts:76`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/kem.ts:76`, BLS12-381 `src/crypto/group.ts:1`, HKDF `src/ui/vectors.ts:185`, Pairing `src/crypto/group.ts:41`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/kem.ts:46`
- **Source review:** [5780db419dd5](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-rekey-relay/commit/5780db419dd548127908286d19b146057329b301) — Bounded source review of README, proxy schemes, group/KEM bridge, vectors, undelegation and actual UI callers. BBS98 here is Blaze-Bleumer-Strauss proxy re-encryption, not the Boneh-Boyen-Shacham BBS credential-signature scheme: src/ui/vectors.ts:296 calls bbs98.encrypt. src/crypto/group.ts:1 imports the BLS12-381 namespace for G1/G2/GT and pairing operations, not BLS signing or verification. Exclude those two false signature credits and apparent signature references while preserving real BLS12-381, Pairing, HKDF, SHA-256 and AES-GCM operations. src/ui/undelegate.ts:96 cites another paper on chosen-ciphertext security; src/main.ts:189 describes an unreproduced discrete-log reduction. Neither is an executed attack. Preserve actual proxy collusion, key recovery, delegation composition and revocation-limit exhibits without inventing vocabulary entries for them. This review does not certify the Type-3 adaptation, constant-time execution, security or new test results; application source is unchanged. Fleet relationship finding relationship:crypto-lab-credential-veil:crypto-lab-rekey-relay, work719fceef-dd13-498a-9343-a55117c50e76.
- **References:** Boneh-Franklin IBE, Diffie-Hellman, EC point arithmetic, ElGamal, Schnorr
