- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [934deba71b3e](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-rekey-relay/commit/934deba71b3e6217d8aff8b734482c8696413a46) reviewed 2026-10-22; 6 mapped sections.

### Reshare Circle

[`crypto-lab-reshare-circle`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-reshare-circle/) · Proactive Secret Sharing · MPC & THRESHOLD

Refresh threshold shares into a new epoch: every old share becomes garbage, the public key never changes, and the secret is never reconstructed along the way.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Shamir, Feldman VSS, HJKY 1995, Mobile Adversary — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **References:** ECDSA, EdDSA, FROST, ML-DSA, RSA
- **Attacks shown:** Discrete log `src/ui/intro.ts:24`
- **Standards body:** —
- **Implementation:** hand-rolled
- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [bdba3dc208b0](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-reshare-circle/commit/bdba3dc208b0bf347e9f06e20f001dbec2b7f3f5) reviewed 2026-10-22; 6 mapped sections.
  - **Advance an epoch while retaining the same secret** (`advance-epoch`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** 1 · Turn the epoch — same secret, brand-new shares
    - **Learner action:** Advance a 3-of-5 sharing and inspect old and new shares and full dealing audit.
    - **Observed result:** Each share changes while the reconstructed secret and public key remain equal.
    - **Concepts taught:** proactive secret sharing; zero-constant refresh polynomial; Shamir sharing; epoch
    - **Limits:** One browser simulates custodian channels and exposes secret audit state for pedagogy.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui/circle.ts:27`, `src/ui/circle.ts:118`, `src/ui/circle.ts:155`, `src/ui/circle.ts:201`, `src/reshare/reshare.ts:1`
  - **Reshare 3-of-5 into 4-of-7 membership** (`committee-change`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** 6 · Rotate the committee — 3-of-5 becomes 4-of-7
    - **Learner action:** Run committee and threshold rotation.
    - **Observed result:** Checks the same public key with new shares and enforces the new 4-of-7 threshold.

### Residue Gate

[`crypto-lab-residue-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-residue-gate/) · Quadratic Residuosity · ENCRYPTION, ATTACKS

Compare public Jacobi symbols with private residue classes, encrypt bits, and turn a Rabin decryption oracle into independently verified factors.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Jacobi Symbol, Goldwasser–Micali, Rabin Encryption, Chosen-Ciphertext Attack — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Goldwasser–Micali `src/gm/gm.ts:3`, Jacobi symbol `src/nt/jacobi.ts:4`, Miller–Rabin `src/nt/primes.ts:3`, Rabin encryption `src/rabin/oracle.ts:9`, Tonelli–Shanks `src/nt/sqrt.ts:7`
- **Source review:** [d1f1c553da40](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-residue-gate/commit/d1f1c553da40f36f1f02b57800262271278f441a) — Read binary Jacobi, Euler Legendre, modular roots/CRT, Goldwasser–Micali encryption and the Rabin key-holder closure. The Tonelli anchor executes order halving; the Rabin anchor actually squares the validated message. A public attacker receives N and one root-query closure, never p/q. The canonical QR root oracle yields independently verified factors; redundancy can refuse or accidentally admit a query and is not called CCA security. One-bit Rabin is distinct from GM. Cocks IBE is an extension mention, not Boneh–Franklin IBE. All 17 units, six browser claims, two accessibility views and six mutations passed at the code-identical deployment; this pin changes only integration documentation.
- **References:** Paillier, RSA, RSA-OAEP
- **Attacks shown:** Chosen-ciphertext attack `src/main.ts:1`, Ciphertext malleability `README.md:15`, Factoring `src/main.ts:24`
- **Standards body:** —
- **Implementation:** local BigInt arithmetic / isolated key-holder worker
- **Overlaps:** `crypto-lab-hidden-bit` — Hidden Bit studies hard-core predicates; Residue Gate computes quadratic residues, Goldwasser–Micali ciphertexts and a Rabin root-oracle factoring reduction. crypto-lab-factor-forge: Factor Forge searches for factors directly; Residue Gate exposes the decryption-oracle assumption that yields them.
- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [d1f1c553da40](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-residue-gate/commit/d1f1c553da40f36f1f02b57800262271278f441a) reviewed 2026-10-22; 5 mapped sections.
  - **Goldwasser–Micali Bit Encryption** (`gm`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** One encrypted group element per bit
    - **Learner action:** Enter bits, encrypt twice, decrypt, and multiply a ciphertext by a public pseudosquare.
    - **Observed result:** Randomized encryptions differ while decryption recovers the bits; ciphertext multiplication flips a bit without an integrity check.
    - **Concepts taught:** Goldwasser–Micali; probabilistic encryption; XOR homomorphism; malleability
    - **Limits:** The small shared modulus is a teaching fixture and must not be used as a real key.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:15`, `src/gm/gm.ts:1`
  - **Jacobi +1 Challenge** (`jacobi`; interactive; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Jacobi +1 leaves two possibilities
    - **Learner action:** Draw a challenge for a small composite modulus, guess its class, then reveal factors and full grid.
    - **Observed result:** The public +1 symbol admits both square and pseudosquare classes that the factors distinguish.
    - **Concepts taught:** Jacobi symbol; quadratic residuosity assumption; pseudosquare
    - **Limits:** The toy moduli 77 and 437 are too small to provide security.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:9`, `src/nt/jacobi.ts:1`
  - **Rabin Chosen-Ciphertext Factor Recovery** (`oracle`; interactive; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Ask for one root. Recover the factors.
    - **Learner action:** Send x² to either oracle rule or measure 100 random queries, then compute gcd from an unexpected root.
    - **Observed result:** The canonical-root rule can disclose a factor; redundancy refusals and accidental toy matches are reported separately.
    - **Concepts taught:** Rabin CCA; factoring equivalence; decryption oracle; gcd
    - **Limits:** An oracle refusal stops that query, not all attacks; the toy redundancy and key sharing with Goldwasser–Micali are pedagogical.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:21`, `src/attack/cca.ts:1`, `src/rabin/oracle.ts:1`
  - **Squares and Roots Modulo a Prime** (`prime-roots`; interactive; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Half of the nonzero values are squares
    - **Learner action:** Choose a small prime and value, find modular roots, and square them back.
    - **Observed result:** The trace and residue table show which nonzero values are quadratic residues and how roots come in ± pairs.
    - **Concepts taught:** quadratic residue; Legendre symbol; modular square root
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:8`, `src/nt/sqrt.ts:1`, `src/nt/legendre.ts:1`
  - **Rabin Four Roots and One-Bit Construction** (`rabin`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Squaring is easy. Which root was the message?
    - **Learner action:** Choose redundancy or canonical-root decryption, encrypt and decrypt, and open the randomized one-bit variant.
    - **Observed result:** The four modular roots reveal why decryption needs a disambiguation rule; the one-bit form demonstrates its different CPA claim.
    - **Concepts taught:** Rabin encryption; four square roots; redundancy; chosen-plaintext security
    - **Limits:** Redundancy is not a chosen-ciphertext security proof; the one-bit construction claims CPA security under its assumptions only.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/main.ts:17`, `src/rabin/rabin.ts:1`

### Search Vault

[`crypto-lab-search-vault`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-search-vault/) · Searchable Encryption · PRIVACY, ATTACKS

Real single-keyword SSE, bounded two-keyword OXT, and Type-3 BLS12-381 PEKS side by side — compare query transcripts, run leakage inference and exposed-trapdoor guessing, then test completeness and freshness against a malicious server.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** SSE, OXT, PEKS, BLS12-381, Leakage Abuse, Query Integrity — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/core/aead.ts:14`, AES-GCM `src/core/aead.ts:65`, BLS12-381 `src/peks/core.ts:19`, Hash-to-curve `src/peks/core.ts:109`, HMAC `src/core/prf.ts:25`, OXT `src/oxt/core.ts:226`, Pairing `src/peks/core.ts:137`, PEKS `src/peks/core.ts:113`, ristretto255 `src/oxt/core.ts:22`, SHA-256 `src/core/prf.ts:37`, SHA-512 `src/core/prf.ts:46`
- **Source review:** [d904972690e1](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-search-vault/commit/d904972690e1514d70d5f36fc25b75840b0e4590) — Read the complete merged README, SSE, query-integrity, PEKS and OXT source, tests, learner interface, primary-source boundaries and visible limitations at this exact main commit. The static SSE still executes HMAC-derived search tokens, AES-256-GCM postings, count and IKK keyword inference, and a client-retained result-integrity checkpoint. The PEKS exhibit retains its Type-3 BLS12-381 adaptation, randomized public tags, deterministic trapdoor, public Test scan and bounded exposed-trapdoor dictionary attack. The new Boolean-search exhibit compares two actual isolated SSE lookups with a static two-distinct-keyword OXT adapter. Five independent keys, framed HMAC-SHA-512 scalar derivation, canonical RFC 9496 ristretto255 operations, shuffled flat TSet rows, AES-GCM identifier ciphertexts and a sorted exact XSet execute the cancellation equation; all 91 keyword pairs in both operand orders are checked against plaintext intersections. Learners observe exact query volume, list sizes, matches, repeated stags and conditional candidate-point equality through overlapping, disjoint, changed-x, repeated-s and identical-query controls. The Path ORAM table is derived arithmetic for N=24, Z=4 and L=5, not an ORAM execution or a claim that ORAM composition hides the OXT transcript. This bounded adapter supports one AND over two known distinct terms, does not transfer the paper's full theorem, and does not establish active-server soundness, completeness or freshness. The original Type-3 PEKS proof and GT-encoding limitations also remain. BLS signatures is still a false positive from an imported module alias, Fault injection is still a false positive from a UI default, and Ed25519 is a reference false positive from noble's ristretto module filename; none is implemented here. Exact-main run 40088072088 passed 180 unit tests and all 37 browser/accessibility tests with zero dependency vulnerabilities, then deployed byte-matching assets.

### Sector Vault

[`crypto-lab-sector-vault`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-sector-vault/) · Disk Encryption · ENCRYPTION

Compare XTS, historical EME2 and AES-GCM on ciphertext edits and rollback. Measure how changes spread, see which modifications are detected, and learn why freshness needs trusted version state.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** XTS-AES, EME2 (historical), Ciphertext Stealing, AES-GCM — labels do not establish what any section runs.

Source is Halevi 2004 Figure 1 and archived IEEE P1619.2/D9 December 2008, not asserted IEEE1619.2-2025 conformance. Independent OpenSSL/BigInt and noble/byte arithmetic checks in both directions, six published third-party self-generated regression vectors with explicit key-order mapping, partial-block/AD/128-block-renewal boundaries and replay controls passed. 159 unit tests, build, 23 browser claim tests and desktop/380px/280px accessibility checks passed locally. XTS/AES-GCM and trusted-version lessons remain. Remove CPA, nonce-reuse and padding-oracle attack credits: these are comparison/limitation prose or sibling-lab links; the lab does not execute those attacks. Ciphertext manipulation and rollback are actual operations. No production, constant-time or current-edition conformance claim. SHA-256 appears only as a retrieved-source fingerprint, not a taught cryptographic primitive.

### Shelf Oracle

[`crypto-lab-shelf-oracle`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-shelf-oracle/) · Single-Server PIR · PRIVACY

Compare direct and compressed full-scan BFV with a separate bounded Piano-style stateful route: client setup streams the database, retains private hints, and reduces online work to eight record probes while exposing refresh, loss and update costs.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** BFV, RLWE, Query Expansion, Noise Budget, Stateful PIR — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** BFV `src/pir/bfv.ts:88`, ChaCha20 `src/pir/chacha20.ts:123`, NTT `src/pir/ntt.ts:61`, Private information retrieval `src/pir/pir.ts:191`, Ring-LWE `src/pir/bfv.ts:88`, SHA-256 `src/pir/records.ts:80`
- **Source review:** [d08691c9e17a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-shelf-oracle/commit/d08691c9e17aaf624781adb127ac4a161f993690) — Read the complete merged README, source, unit and browser tests, learner interface and visible limitations at this exact main commit. The mature direct path encrypts one selector per record and performs the full BFV plaintext-ciphertext fold. The bounded compressed route serializes four fixed ciphertext blocks, expands each through implemented odd Galois substitutions and noisy binary-gadget key switching, scans all 64 records and returns four fixed responses. Its exact two-prime NTT/CRT products fail closed against a proved coefficient bound; selected compressed, direct and independently built record bytes agree while the other three responses decrypt to zero. The separate bounded Piano-style adaptation streams the static 64-record database during client setup, retains private parity hints, punctured backups and replacement records, then sends an exact eight-byte request whose eight record probes produce one 512-byte parity response. Recovery and backup refresh use the displayed XOR equations; cached repeats spend a distinct effective target and send the same online shape. The 33-request window, 256 primary hints and displayed 33 · (7/8)^249 availability bound are scoped to this fixed independent-coordinate teaching model, not a 128-bit or transferred Piano theorem. Executed ledgers keep setup bytes, retained state, wire bytes, record probes, parity contributions, cache growth, update scans and rebuild work in separate units; they are not timing benchmarks. State loss sends cover without recovery, malformed or abandoned responses invalidate rather than roll back, an external high-water mark detects stale serialized state, and any known database update invalidates the epoch before a full rebuild. The stateful server has no derived ProcessDB artifact, and the lesson does not implement dynamic Piano, authenticated storage, malicious-server integrity or privacy, availability, traffic hiding, ORAM, multi-client sharing, crash consistency, incremental updates, the reference implementation's wire format or asymptotic storage guarantees. The compressed route still does not implement SealPIR multidimensional recursion, sublinear server work, modulus switching, seeded ciphertext compression or production parameter sets, and its key-dependent evaluation material retains the stated circular-security assumption. The SHA-256 record tag and snapshot digest detect accidental decode failure and a locally known change; neither authenticates freshness against a malicious server. Chosen-plaintext attack is an IND-CPA prose match, Keyword inference belongs only to a Search Vault link, and Side-channel is a visible implementation limitation rather than an executed attack. DES is a false match inside a catalog note about the Journal des Debats, and Gaussian mechanism is a false classification of discrete-Gaussian error prose; neither is a Shelf Oracle algorithm reference. Exact-main run 40102100735 passed all 121 unit tests, the production build and all 38 hosted browser/accessibility tests.
- **References:** BGV, LWE, Poly1305, Private set intersection

- **Implementation:** hand-rolled direct/compressed BFV PIR, bounded Piano-style stateful PIR, NTT and ChaCha20; WebCrypto SHA-256
- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [d08691c9e17a](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-shelf-oracle/commit/d08691c9e17aaf624781adb127ac4a161f993690) reviewed 2026-10-24; 11 mapped sections.
  - **Compressed Query Expansion** (`compressed-query-expansion`; comparison; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Compressed Query / Four encrypted blocks in, sixty-four encrypted selectors out
    - **Learner action:** Run direct and compressed retrieval for one fixed-catalog record, then inspect the expansion, cost, noise and discarded one-response ledgers.
    - **Observed result:** Expands four serialized ciphertext blocks into 64 encrypted selectors with Galois key switching; the selected response agrees with direct retrieval and the independently built tagged record while the other three decrypt to zero, and the panel accounts for setup, traffic, fixed responses, record products and switching work.

### SNARK Arena

[`crypto-lab-snark-arena`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-snark-arena/) · Zero-Knowledge Proofs · ZERO-KNOWLEDGE

Generate and verify real BN254 Groth16 proofs, then compare a deliberately weak XOR relation with an in-circuit bit-constrained repair that rejects the same non-binary assignment. Separate toy-field panels demonstrate powers of tau and an accepted KZG opening forged with retained toxic waste; PLONK remains comparison-only.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Groth16, R1CS, Constraint Gap, Trusted Setup, vs. PLONK — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **Source review:** [025f878b22b2](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-snark-arena/commit/025f878b22b2fa3df945359548c2422d9548c1f4) — Re-read the complete cubic, weak-XOR and repaired-XOR Groth16 paths; Circom sources and artifacts; toy-field R1CS/KZG setup and ceremony paths; provenance, mutation, browser and unit controls; README; and current main through this exact pin. The weak public-input relation accepts an unmodified proof for (a,b,out)=(2,2,r-4) because it encodes only out=a+b-2ab. The repaired relation adds in-circuit a(a-1)=b(b-1)=0 constraints, uses regenerated circuit-specific WASM/zkey/verification-key material and rejects that assignment while retaining all four binary rows. A browser input check is not the repair, ordinary proof-element tampering is a separate rejected control, and these public inputs establish neither secret nor key recovery. Real cubic proof mechanics disclose the bounded witness through public output; PLONK remains comparison-only. The executable toy KZG lesson forges an opening when the toxic scalar is retained, but the current attack vocabulary has no honest term for that specific failure; discrete-log wording names a hardness assumption rather than an executed attack. Authenticated Circom 2.2.3 rebuilds reproduce all three shipped witness WASM files and bind the XOR R1CS/PTAU/zkey/vkey material, but the single-party demo ceremony, secret destruction and vendored snarkjs source reproduction remain unverified. This bounded CL098 adaptation does not implement CCC-Check, reproduce its evaluation or establish universal circuit correctness. Preserve raw WebAssembly scanner coverage separately.

### SPDZ Forge

[`crypto-lab-spdz-forge`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-spdz-forge/) · Malicious-Secure MPC · PROTOCOLS, MPC & THRESHOLD

Run authenticated sharing, Beaver multiplication, and ordinary tamper detection over F_p (2^61−1). A separate bounded Off-Key fixture contrasts consistent α with β=α+Δ preprocessing, deriving unmasked secret recovery and a masked one-bit selective-failure result from protocol state.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** SPDZ, Beaver Triples, SPDZ MACs, Dishonest Majority, Selective Failure — labels do not establish what any section runs.

- **Source review:** [2bfdc83b0ef5](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-spdz-forge/commit/2bfdc83b0ef587a598afad95d6ef0e72bdfd904b) — Read the complete three-party trusted-dealer SPDZ engine, Off-Key extension, UI, tests and README through this exact pin and checked the bounded adaptation against CL079 Sections 3, 3.2, 4.1-4.5, 5 and 5.1. Additive sharing, Beaver multiplication and information-theoretic MAC arithmetic are local BigInt TypeScript; WebCrypto supplies SHA-256 commitments and randomness rather than the whole protocol implementation. The isolated fixture computes the consistent-context residual Delta(g-d) and inconsistent-context residual Delta(g-y) from actual authenticated shares, then derives unmasked recovery and masked bit-promise inference from attacker-visible state without exposing y or honest shares. Its omniscient audit is separately labeled, ordinary corruption remains a correctness control, and the same-context comparison restores the modeled assumption through protocol state rather than client-side validation. Credit the executable selective-failure lesson, not generic key recovery: y is a shared input, not a cryptographic key. This is a three-party trusted-dealer, nonzero-mu, unbatched algebraic adaptation, not a reproduction of distributed preprocessing, persistence, concurrency or an evaluated framework.

### Split Point

[`crypto-lab-split-point`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-split-point/) · Function Secret Sharing · PROTOCOLS, MPC & THRESHOLD

Secret-share a function, not a value: two DPF keys each evaluate to shares of one-at-α, zero everywhere else. Two non-colluding servers fold 65,536 records and neither learns which one you read.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** DPF, 2-Server PIR, AES-128-CTR, FSS — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/dpf/prg.ts:1`, Private information retrieval `src/ui/app.ts:9`
- **Standards body:** NIST
- **Implementation:** @noble
- **Exhibit map:** COMPLETE SOURCE REVIEW. Source pin [e0b0a2d565e9](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-split-point/commit/e0b0a2d565e9668af3ad2d9a32889296e4a22dda) reviewed 2026-10-22; 5 mapped sections.
  - **Server Answer Tampering** (`answer-tamper`; interactive; simulation)
    - **Visible section:** PRIVACY IS NOT INTEGRITY
    - **Learner action:** Enable one-server bit flip and fetch again.
    - **Observed result:** Shows corrupted returned record and the outside teaching oracle detects its difference from shelf[alpha].
    - **Concepts taught:** PIR integrity; malicious server; unauthenticated answer
    - **Limits:** The protocol itself has no verifier for malicious answers.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `index.html:137`, `index.html:157`, `index.html:160`, `index.html:162`, `src/attack/tamper.ts:1`
  - **Two-Key Collusion Break** (`collusion`; interactive; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Break the non-collusion assumption

### Stego Suite

[`crypto-lab-stego-suite`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-stego-suite/) · Steganography · STEGANOGRAPHY

Compare LSB, DCT, and adaptive image hiding with chi-squared steganalysis. Optional AES-GCM passphrase encryption versions its KDF and warns when opening legacy images.

Runs the real SynthID-Text keyed detector over watermarked text, then signs the same words with ECDSA P-256: change only the key and the statistical evidence vanishes; change one byte and verification fails outright.

### Traitor Trace

[`crypto-lab-traitor-trace`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-traitor-trace/) · Broadcast Encryption · ENCRYPTION, PROTOCOLS

Naor-Naor-Lotspiech subset-cover over a 16-leaf tree — one ciphertext for all subscribers, revoke a member without rekeying anyone, and trace a leaked decoder back to its builder. Real AES-256-GCM.

  - **Test pooled keys and evasive tracing** (`collusion`; interactive; real-crypto)

### WEP Crack

[`crypto-lab-wep-crack`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-wep-crack/) · A Cipher Inside a Broken Protocol · ENCRYPTION, ATTACKS, HISTORICAL

Run real RC4 inside WEP protected bodies, observe IV reuse, forge a message by repairing its CRC-32, and attempt bounded PTW key recovery using only traffic generated in the browser.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** RC4, WEP Protected Bodies, CRC-32, PTW — labels do not establish what any section runs.

Generated traffic only, not complete 802.11 frames or a real-network capture tool. The RC4 anchor points to the keystream engine rather than a UI type. Chosen-ciphertext attack was picked from a build brief and Padding oracle from a sibling link, neither a demonstrated oracle attack here; remove those credits. CRC-32 ciphertext forgery and bounded probabilistic PTW recovery are actual computations; exact key equality is checked separately. 149 unit, 2 accessibility and 49 claims/interaction tests passed.

### What Is PQC

[`crypto-lab-what-is-pqc`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-what-is-pqc/) · Post-Quantum Basics · POST-QUANTUM, KEY EXCHANGE

Runs a real ML-KEM-768 exchange beside a real X25519 one in matching panels, so the only measurable difference is size &mdash; 2,272 bytes on the wire instead of 64. Not stronger: a different hard problem.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** ML-KEM-768, X25519, FIPS 203, Size, Not Strength — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** ML-KEM `src/exchange/mlkem.ts:39`, X25519 `src/exchange/x25519.ts:38`
- **Source review:** [193e2248a953](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-what-is-pqc/commit/193e2248a9530e88a0b88ebcd78537cce20832c3) — Read src/exchange/mlkem.ts and x25519.ts. Both algorithms are real: ml_kem768.keygen / encapsulate / decapsulate from @noble/post-quantum, and x25519.getPublicKey / scalar multiplication from @noble/curves. The scanner anchored both at line 1, which is the IMPORT line in each file; the pins above move them to the operations, so the index points at work rather than at a dependency. The derived attack anchor 'Factoring@README.md:50' is prose in the README explaining why today's keys fall, not an attack this lab mounts. CORRECTED 2026-10-06: this note said it was not carried and it was -- `add` replaces anchors but does not drop a derived attack, which takes `remove`. The remove list below now does what the sentence claimed. The lab's own argument is that ML-KEM is not STRONGER than X25519 but rests on a different hard problem, with the measurable difference being size on the wire.

### X3DH Wire

[`crypto-lab-x3dh-wire`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/) · Asynchronous Key Agreement · KEY EXCHANGE, PROTOCOLS

Explore classical X3DH with real X25519, three required DH terms, an optional fourth one-time prekey term, and HKDF. Replace a whole signed bundle to see why Bob’s identity key must be authenticated independently.

  - **Alice Initiates Asynchronously** (`alice-init`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 2: Alice Initiates
    - **Learner action:** Advance to Alice’s fresh identity and ephemeral keys and the fetched public prekey bundle while Bob is offline.
    - **Observed result:** The panel shows which public fields Alice receives before computing the first-session DH terms.
    - **Concepts taught:** asynchronous key agreement; ephemeral key; prekey bundle
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:287`, `src/ui.ts:290`, `src/ui.ts:293`, `src/ui.ts:300`
  - **Corrupt Alice's ephemeral key on the wire** (`corrupt-ephemeral-key`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Flip a byte of the transmitted EK_A public key and follow Bob's derivation and initial-message decryption.
    - **Observed result:** The independently computed secrets diverge and AES-GCM authentication fails at Bob.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; ephemeral Diffie-Hellman; key agreement failure; AEAD authentication
    - **Limits:** The initial-message demonstration omits X3DH's identity-key associated data, explicitly disclosed in src/ui.ts:628.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:202`, `src/x3dh.ts:292`, `src/x3dh.ts:309`, `src/x3dh.ts:314`, `src/ui.ts:624`
  - **Initial AES-GCM Message and Ratchet Handoff** (`first-message`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 5: Handoff to Double Ratchet
    - **Learner action:** Inspect transmitted public fields, IV and ciphertext and Bob’s decryption outcome.
    - **Observed result:** The panel shows the derived SK protecting the first message before Double Ratchet handoff.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH initial message; AES-GCM; Double Ratchet
    - **Limits:** The demo omits the spec’s identity-associated data, weakening context binding.

  - **X3DH Diffie-Hellman Terms and Commutativity** (`four-dh`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 3: Four DH Operations
    - **Learner action:** Toggle Alice and Bob views, compare DH2’s two computations, regenerate keys and inspect DH1 through DH4.
    - **Observed result:** With matching keys, both endpoints derive identical 32-byte leg outputs; an absent OPK drops DH4.
    - **Concepts taught:** X25519; DH1; DH2; DH3; DH4; commutativity
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:432`, `src/ui.ts:440`, `src/ui.ts:478`, `src/ui.ts:483`, `src/ui.ts:492`
  - **Concatenated DH Material to Session Key** (`kdf-sk`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 4: KDF → Shared Secret
    - **Learner action:** Inspect F and the computed DH blocks entering HKDF-SHA-256 and compare Alice and Bob session keys.
    - **Observed result:** The output shows byte equality or a highlighted difference when tampered inputs change a DH term.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH key schedule; domain separation; HKDF-SHA-256; shared secret
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:547`, `src/ui.ts:555`, `src/ui.ts:576`, `src/ui.ts:580`, `src/ui.ts:596`
  - **Signed Prekey Bundle and Identity Pin** (`key-registry`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Panel 1: Key Registry — offered prekey bundle
    - **Learner action:** Inspect Bob’s published key bundle, XEdDSA signed prekey and offered-versus-trusted identity fingerprint.
    - **Observed result:** The verifier authenticates the prekey under an offered identity; an independently established pin is needed to know the identity belongs to Bob.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; XEdDSA; signed prekey; identity pin; safety number
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:239`, `src/ui.ts:244`, `src/ui.ts:249`, `src/ui.ts:256`, `src/ui.ts:265`

    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Toggle off Bob's one-time prekey and examine the DH set and status strip.
    - **Observed result:** The fourth DH term is omitted, while Alice and Bob can still derive a matching shared secret.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; one-time prekeys; DH4; asynchronous key agreement; forward secrecy
    - **Limits:** This teaching contrast does not constitute a forward-secrecy proof.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:201`, `src/ui.ts:227`, `src/x3dh.ts:275`, `src/x3dh.ts:300`
  - **Replace the whole prekey bundle** (`replace-whole-bundle`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Offer a different identity key and its correctly signed prekey, then compare the offered fingerprint with a previously trusted Bob fingerprint.
    - **Observed result:** The signature can remain valid while the identity pin mismatches. The deliberately unpinned continuation lets the attacker derive the same session key and decrypt the first message.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; identity verification; out-of-band key comparison; active impersonation; bundle substitution
    - **Limits:** The trusted fingerprint is a teaching fixture; real users must authenticate identities independently. The unpinned continuation demonstrates the failure and is not a secure protocol path.
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:200`, `src/ui.ts:253`, `src/x3dh.ts:251`, `src/x3dh.ts:302`, `src/x3dh.ts:323`, `src/ui.ts:625`
  - **Tamper the signed prekey signature** (`tamper-signed-prekey`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Flip the SPK signature byte or substitute an attacker-signed SPK while Bob's identity key remains in the bundle.
    - **Observed result:** XEdDSA verification fails and the X3DH handshake aborts before deriving a shared secret or sending a message.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; signed prekeys; XEdDSA; prekey-bundle substitution; signature verification
    - **Evidence at pinned commit:** `src/ui.ts:198`, `src/ui.ts:199`, `src/x3dh.ts:273`, `src/x3dh.ts:279`, `src/ui.ts:210`
